Subject: SIG follow-up + retention question

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for turning around the SIG draft so quickly. A couple of our security reviewers flagged question 4.2 (Operational logging and retention). Their expectation is a standard answer: "Audit logs are retained for 30 days by default; longer retention available by request."

Looking at your draft you note "operational and request logs are retained for up to 90 days for troubleshooting and billing reconciliation." That is outside our baseline and will need an internal exception or exec-level approval to accept.

Can you confirm whether the 90-day retention is fixed, configurable per customer, or if there is a short-term product roadmap to add shorter retention windows? If we get exec confirmation that this is configurable or can be made shorter, I can close this item on our side.

Appreciate the quick turnaround—we're trying to keep the review moving this week.

Best,
Megan

FinCorp Capital

Megan — thanks for flagging.

Short answer: the current production behavior is that operational logs (request traces, inference telemetry) are persisted for up to 90 days to support debugging and billing reconciliation. We have controls to restrict access and to purge customer-identifiable data on shorter timelines, but the default window is 90 days.

We're aware this is a common point of friction. I'm looping in Dylan (sales/solutions) and Marissa (product compliance) to propose an acceptable position for the SIG. If needed, we may need an executive confirmation for a one-time exception or a product commitment to add a configurable retention toggle.

Proposed next steps:
- Dylan: propose a customer-facing phrasing that minimizes risk while keeping us honest.
- Marissa/Jonas: confirm whether a short-term configuration or documented exception is feasible (timeline/cost).
- If not feasible, I'll request an exec decision and capture it in writing for FinCorp's auditors.

Hannah

Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — quick note from the GTM side.

FinCorp is on the procurement path and pushing for SOC- and SIG-aligned baseline controls. They will escalate if the SIG answer is a hard "90 days only." We should avoid contract blockers.

I suggest the following customer-facing phrasing we can use in the SIG draft: 
"Operational logs (used for debugging, telemetry, and billing reconciliation) are retained up to 90 days by default. Customers may request shorter retention windows through our support/contract process, subject to reasonable operational constraints."

This keeps us flexible while giving FinCorp an explicit path to a shorter window. If product/legal want a stronger guarantee (e.g., a configurable toggle within 30 days), that will require a roadmap commitment and likely exec sign-off for contractual exceptions.

If Product can sign off on the phrasing, I'll push this as the final SIG answer and request that FinCorp acknowledges it in the questionnaire.

-Dylan

Looping in Product/Engineering specifics.

Short technical clarifications:
- The 90-day retention is currently an operational default in our logging pipeline.
- We already support selective redaction of PII fields before longer-term persistence; that is in production.
- A per-customer configurable retention policy (e.g., 30-day toggle) is not available today — building it is medium effort because it touches the ingestion/retention job and billing reconciliation windows. Rough estimate: 6–10 weeks with a small eng team, plus testing and runbook updates.

Given that timeline, we have two pragmatic options:
1) Sign the SIG with Dylan's phrasing (default 90 days, shorter by request via support/contract) — requires exec acknowledgement for customers expecting a baseline 30-day retention.
2) Commit to a roadmap item with a clear timeline (we can offer a formal product commitment with milestones) — requires prioritization and an exec-level resource/time commitment to push it into the next sprint cycle.

I'll start a Jira ticket (INF-7894) to track the engineering work if we opt for #2. If you want me to include cost/PM estimates for the sales thread, I can do that.

—Marissa
Director, Product Compliance & Strategy
Redwood Inference
